author: Will Durant, Ariel Durant

title: Babel

title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone

He must attend a famous school of magic and sorcery, where he establishes a friendship with two young men who will become his companions on his adventure. During his first year at Hogwarts, he discovers that a malevolent and powerful wizard named Voldemort is in search of a philosopher's stone that prolongs the life of its owner.
author: J.K. Rowling

title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets

title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire

author: J.K. Rowling

title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
description: In his fifth year at Hogwarts, Harry discovers that many members of the wizarding community do not know the truth about his encounter with Lord Voldemort. Cornelius Fudge, Minister of Magic, appoints Dolores Umbridge as Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher because he believes that Professor Dumbledore plans to take over his job. But his teachings are inadequate, so Harry prepares the students to defend the school against evil.
author: J.K. Rowling

title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
description: Harry discovers a powerful book and, while trying to discover its origins, collaborates with Dumbledore in the search for a series of magical objects that will aid in the destruction of Lord Voldemort.
author: J.K. Rowling

title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
description: Harry, Ron and Hermione go on a dangerous mission to locate and destroy the secret of Voldemort's immortality and destruction - the Horcruces. Alone, without the guidance of their teachers or the protection of Professor Dumbledore, the three friends must lean on each other more than ever. But there are Dark Forces in between that threaten to tear them apart. Harry Potter is getting closer and closer to the task for which he has been preparing since the first day he set foot in Hogwarts: the last battle with Voldemort.
author: J.K. Rowling

title: Harry Potter and the Cursed Child

author: Inio Asano

author: Osamu Dazai

author: Annie Ernaux

description: Milton and Rose Friedman explain their views on individual freedom, economic choice, markets, government, and personal responsibility.
author: Milton Friedman

author: Leo Tolstoy

title: The Unbearable Lightness of Being
description: A philosophical novel about love, infidelity, freedom, political upheaval, and the weight or lightness of human existence.
author: Milan Kundera

The book also focuses on his long and distinguished cinematic career.
author: Luis Buñuel

title: Astronomy Made Simple

title: The Masnavi

title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
description: A landmark work of philosophy and literature, Thus Spoke Zarathustra is the fullest expression of Nietzsche's belief in the development of humanity through its highest individuals. Zarathustra, the archetypal Übermensch, leaves his home for the mountains and explores ideas beyond conventional standards of good and evil.

title: Crime and Punishment

Having accomplished the deed, Raskolnikov struggles with mental anguish while trying to avoid the consequences and hide his guilt from his friends and family.
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
description: A novel that narrates the vicissitudes of Aureliano Buendía in the mythical town of Macondo. The story follows the Buendía family across seven generations and blends elements of fiction and reality in the style of magical realism.
author: Gabriel García Márquez

title: A Game of Thrones
description: An epic fantasy novel set in Westeros, where powerful families struggle for the Iron Throne amid political intrigue, betrayal, war, loyalty, and supernatural threats.

description: A philosophical novel about Meursault, an emotionally detached man whose life is transformed by a violent act, exploring absurdity, alienation, death, and society's expectations.
author: Albert Camus

title: Blindness
description: A mysterious epidemic of blindness spreads rapidly through a city, forcing people into quarantine and exposing the darkest and most primitive aspects of human behavior, survival, morality, and society.
author: José Saramago

title: Metamorphosis
author: Franz Kafka
description: Gregor Samsa wakes one morning to find himself inexplicably transformed into a monstrous insect. As he struggles to adapt to his new existence, his relationship with his family deteriorates, exploring alienation, isolation, identity, guilt, and the conditional nature of human relationships.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
description: Viktor Frankl's memoir of his experiences in Nazi concentration camps and his development of logotherapy. The book examines suffering, survival, freedom, responsibility, and the human search for meaning, arguing that people can choose how they respond to even the most difficult circumstances.
author: Viktor E. Frankl

title: The Gadfly
